n: First day of the creation week, three days before the calendar's first Nisan 1.

t: Creation Day 4: sun, moon and stars — the calendar begins
n: The luminaries are made 'for signs and seasons, days and years'; the DSS calendar counts from this Wednesday.
God rests on the seventh day and blesses it.
The fountains of the deep break open in Noah's 600th year, second month, seventeenth day — a Sunday at mid-spring on this calendar.

t: The ark rests on the mountains of Ararat
n: Seventh month, seventeenth day.

t: Tops of the mountains are seen
n: Tenth month, first day.

t: Waters dried from the earth; Noah removes the ark's covering
n: First day of the first month of Noah's 601st year.

t: Earth fully dry; Noah leaves the ark
n: Second month, twenty-seventh day.
Year from the Genesis 11 genealogy; the day is the one given by dsscalendar.org.
430 years to the day before the Exodus.
The lamb is slain on the fourteenth day of the first month.
Israel leaves Rameses the day after Passover.
First day of the first month of the second year after the Exodus.
The cloud lifts from the Tabernacle in the second year, second month, twentieth day.

t: Death of Aaron on Mount Hor
n: Fortieth year after the Exodus, fifth month, first day.
Fortieth year, eleventh month, first day.
Tenth day of the first month; camp at Gilgal.

t: Passover at Gilgal; the manna ends
n: First Passover in the land of Canaan.
Day as given by dsscalendar.org; Scripture gives the 7th (2 Kings 25:8) and 10th (Jeremiah 52:12) of the fifth month.
Year from DSS 11Q13 as read by dsscalendar.org; on this calendar Passover always falls on a Tuesday.
Justinian issued the first edition of his consolidated code of imperial law, which went on to underpin much of later European civil law.
The rebuilt Great Church of Constantinople was consecrated less than six years after the Nika riots destroyed its predecessor.
The fifth ecumenical council met to condemn the Three Chapters and continued sitting until 2 June 553.

t: Third Council of Toledo opens; Visigoths renounce Arianism
n: King Reccared and the Visigothic nobility formally embraced Catholic Christianity at this council; some sources give 8 May for the opening.

t: Gregory the Great consecrated Bishop of Rome
n: Gregory, elected after Pelagius II died of plague, was consecrated and later sent the mission of Augustine to the English.

t: Hijra: Muhammad arrives at Quba near Medina
n: Tradition dates the arrival to Monday 8 Rabi al-Awwal; Julian conversions vary by a few days (20 to 24 September), while the Islamic era itself is counted from 16 July 622.
The Muslims of Medina defeated a larger Meccan force on 17 Ramadan AH 2; the Julian date is a calendar conversion.
Muhammad died in Medina, and Abu Bakr was chosen as the first caliph.

t: Battle of Yarmouk ends in Arab victory
n: The decisive day of a battle lasting several days, in which Rashidun forces broke Byzantine power in Syria.

t: Battle of Karbala; Husayn ibn Ali killed
n: Husayn, grandson of Muhammad, was killed on 10 Muharram AH 61, remembered every year at Ashura.
The sixth ecumenical council, held in the domed Trullus hall of the palace, condemned Monothelitism.
Charles Martel's Franks stopped an Umayyad army; the 10 October date is traditional and some scholars prefer 733.
The English missionary bishop who evangelised much of Germany was killed with companions in Frisia; 5 June is his feast and traditional death day.
An Lushan marched out of Fanyang against the Tang court, starting a war that devastated the dynasty.
The seventh ecumenical council restored the veneration of icons, setting out its definition on 13 October.
Norse raiders sacked the island monastery, usually taken as the start of the Viking Age; one chronicle copy says 8 January instead.
Pope Leo III crowned the Frankish king emperor of the Romans at Christmas Mass in St Peter's.

t: Charter founding the Abbey of Cluny
n: Duke William of Aquitaine endowed a monastery free of lay control, which became the centre of a major monastic reform; some date the charter to 909.
Pope John XII crowned Otto in Rome, founding what came to be called the Holy Roman Empire.
Brian Boru defeated Leinster and Norse forces on Good Friday but was killed in the fighting.

t: Humbert lays excommunication on Hagia Sophia altar
n: The papal legate placed a bull against Patriarch Michael Cerularius on the altar, the act usually taken as the start of the East-West Schism.
William of Normandy defeated and killed King Harold II, opening the Norman Conquest.

t: William the Conqueror crowned at Westminster
n: William was crowned king on Christmas Day in Westminster Abbey.
The Seljuk sultan Alp Arslan defeated and captured Emperor Romanos IV, opening Anatolia to Turkish settlement.
After standing as a penitent at the castle gate, the excommunicated king was absolved by Pope Gregory VII.

t: Urban II calls the First Crusade at Clermont
n: Pope Urban II preached in a field outside Clermont, urging Christians to go to the aid of the East and to Jerusalem.
Crusaders broke into the city after a siege of about five weeks and massacred many of its inhabitants.
Emperor Henry V and Pope Callixtus II settled the Investiture Controversy over who appoints bishops.

t: Thomas Becket murdered in Canterbury Cathedral
n: Four knights of Henry II killed the archbishop in his cathedral, and he was canonised within three years.
Saladin destroyed the army of the Kingdom of Jerusalem near Tiberias, opening the way to Jerusalem.
The city surrendered to Saladin after a short siege, ending 88 years of crusader rule.
Crusaders broke into the Christian capital and sacked it over three days, deepening the split between East and West.
King John agreed to the charter of liberties put to him by rebel barons.
Innocent III's great council defined transubstantiation and required annual confession and communion.

t: Honorius III approves the Dominican Order
n: The bull Religiosam vitam confirmed Dominic's community of preachers at Toulouse.

t: Franciscan Rule approved by papal bull
n: Honorius III confirmed the final Rule of Francis of Assisi with the bull Solet annuere.

t: Abbasid caliph surrenders Baghdad to Hulagu
n: Caliph al-Musta'sim surrendered to the Mongols, who began sacking the city three days later.
The Mamluks of Egypt defeated a Mongol army in Galilee, halting the Mongol advance toward Egypt.

t: Boniface VIII proclaims the first Jubilee
n: The bull Antiquorum habet offered a plenary indulgence to pilgrims to Rome and began the Holy Year tradition.
Robert the Bruce defeated Edward II on the second day of the battle, securing Scottish independence for a generation.
Scottish nobles wrote to Pope John XXII asserting Scotland's independence and asking him to recognise Robert the Bruce as king.

t: Zhu Yuanzhang proclaims the Ming dynasty
n: At Nanjing, Zhu proclaimed himself emperor as the Hongwu Emperor, and his forces drove the Mongol Yuan from Beijing later that year.
Archbishop Courtenay's council condemned Wycliffe's teachings while an earthquake shook London.
The Czech reformer was condemned by the Council of Constance and executed despite a promise of safe conduct.
Henry V's outnumbered English army, relying on its longbowmen, defeated the French on St Crispin's Day.

t: Martin V elected, ending the Western Schism
n: The Council of Constance chose Oddone Colonna as the single pope, closing nearly forty years of rival papacies.

t: Joan of Arc burned at Rouen
n: After a church trial under English control, Joan was burned as a relapsed heretic; she was cleared in 1456 and canonised in 1920.

t: Council of Florence decrees union with the Greeks
n: The decree Laetentur caeli announced a reunion of the Latin and Greek churches, which was later rejected in the East.

t: Fall of Constantinople to the Ottomans
n: Mehmed II's army stormed the walls, ending the Byzantine Empire, and Hagia Sophia became a mosque.

t: Mainz Psalter completed, first dated printed book
n: Fust and Schoeffer's colophon dates the book to the eve of the Assumption and is the first to name its printers and date.

t: Kongo king Nzinga a Nkuwu baptised as Joao I
n: The king and his family received baptism from Portuguese priests, beginning Kongo's long Catholic history.

t: Granada surrenders to Ferdinand and Isabella
n: Emir Muhammad XII handed over the city, ending the last Muslim state in Iberia.

t: Alhambra Decree expels Jews from Spain
n: The Catholic Monarchs ordered all practising Jews to convert or leave their kingdoms by the end of July.

t: Columbus makes landfall in the Bahamas
n: Columbus's expedition reached an island the Lucayans called Guanahani; the date is Julian (21 October in the proleptic Gregorian).
Spain and Portugal divided newly found lands outside Europe along a meridian west of the Cape Verde islands.
Da Gama's fleet arrived on the Malabar coast, opening a sea route from Europe to India around Africa.
The Dominican preacher who had dominated Florence was hanged and burned in the Piazza della Signoria.
A Portuguese fleet bound for India sighted Monte Pascoal and claimed the land for Portugal.

t: Montesinos preaches against abuse of the Taino
n: On the fourth Sunday of Advent the Dominican Antonio de Montesinos denounced the colonists' treatment of the native people.
The colophon of Cardinal Cisneros's polyglot dates the first printed Greek New Testament, though the work was not issued until about 1522.
Luther sent his theses against indulgences to Archbishop Albrecht of Mainz; the posting on the Wittenberg church door is traditional.

t: Luther burns the papal bull Exsurge Domine
n: Outside Wittenberg's Elster Gate, Luther burned the bull threatening him with excommunication, along with books of canon law.

t: Luther refuses to recant at the Diet of Worms
n: Before Emperor Charles V, Luther declined to retract his writings unless refuted by Scripture and plain reason.
Cuauhtemoc was captured and the Aztec capital fell to Cortes and his Tlaxcalan and other Indigenous allies after a long siege.
Elcano brought the last ship of Magellan's expedition into Sanlucar de Barrameda with 18 survivors.
Conrad Grebel baptised George Blaurock at Felix Manz's house, usually taken as the founding of the Anabaptist movement.
Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi of the Delhi Sultanate and founded the Mughal Empire.
Suleiman the Magnificent destroyed the Hungarian army, and King Louis II died fleeing the field.
Swiss Brethren meeting under Michael Sattler agreed seven articles that defined early Anabaptist practice.

t: Augsburg Confession presented to Charles V
n: The Lutheran princes had Melanchthon's statement of faith read aloud at the Diet of Augsburg.

t: Our Lady of Guadalupe image revealed (tradition)
n: Catholic tradition holds that Juan Diego showed Bishop Zumarraga the image on his cloak on this day; early documentation is debated.
Spanish forces ambushed the Inca ruler's retinue in Cajamarca's plaza and took him prisoner.
The colophon of Myles Coverdale's translation, the first complete printed English Bible, gives 4 October 1535.
The translator of the English New Testament was strangled and burned for heresy; 6 October is the traditional date.
The bull declared that the Indigenous peoples of the Americas were rational beings who must not be enslaved or robbed.

t: Society of Jesus approved by Paul III
n: The bull Regimini militantis Ecclesiae formally established Ignatius of Loyola's order.
Emperor Gelawdewos and Portuguese musketeers defeated and killed Ahmad Gran, saving the Christian Ethiopian kingdom; sources differ on the date.
The council that framed the Catholic response to the Reformation held its first session.

t: First Book of Common Prayer comes into use
n: Cranmer's English liturgy became mandatory on Whitsunday, sparking the Prayer Book Rebellion in the West Country.
The Jesuit missionary came ashore with Japanese convert Anjiro, beginning Christian missions in Japan.
The settlement let each prince of the Empire choose Lutheranism or Catholicism for his own territory.

t: Scottish Parliament approves the Scots Confession
n: The Reformation Parliament adopted the Reformed confession drafted by John Knox and five colleagues.
The Holy League's galleys destroyed most of the Ottoman fleet in the Gulf of Patras.
Catholic mobs and royal troops in Paris killed Huguenot leaders and thousands of Protestants, and the killing spread to other cities.
Akechi Mitsuhide's troops attacked the Kyoto temple and Nobunaga took his own life; this is a Julian conversion of the Japanese date (Tensho 10, 6th month, 2nd day).
Following Gregory XIII's bull Inter gravissimas, Catholic lands went straight from Thursday 4 October to Friday 15 October.

t: Battle of Gravelines breaks the Spanish Armada
n: English fireships and guns scattered the Armada off Flanders; this is the English Old Style date, and the Spanish recorded 8 August (New Style).
A Moroccan army armed with firearms defeated Askia Ishaq II, bringing about the collapse of the Songhai Empire.
Henry IV gave French Protestants legal toleration and civil rights, ending the Wars of Religion.
Tokugawa Ieyasu's victory led to the Tokugawa shogunate; this is a conversion of the Japanese date (Keicho 5, 9th month, 15th day).
The Jesuit missionary arrived at the Ming capital and was later allowed to stay there under the Wanli Emperor's patronage.
The Virginia Company settlers came ashore on the James River and built James Fort; the date is Old Style (24 May New Style).
Samuel de Champlain set up his habitation at the narrows of the St Lawrence, the start of Quebec City.
Protestant nobles threw two Catholic imperial regents and their secretary from a window of Prague Castle, triggering the Thirty Years' War.
The international Reformed synod at Dordrecht answered the Remonstrants and produced the Canons of Dort, closing on 9 May 1619.
At anchor off Cape Cod, the Pilgrims and other passengers agreed to form a civil body politic; the date is Old Style (21 November New Style).
Maisonneuve and about fifty settlers founded a missionary colony on the island of Montreal.
The treaties of Munster and Osnabruck ended the Thirty Years' War and recognised Calvinism alongside Lutheranism and Catholicism in the Empire.
The king was beheaded outside the Banqueting House in Whitehall; contemporaries wrote 1648 because their year began on 25 March, and the New Style date is 9 February.
Blaise Pascal recorded an intense religious experience on a parchment he kept sewn into his coat until he died.
About two thousand ministers who would not conform to the Act of Uniformity lost their livings on St Bartholomew's Day (3 September New Style).
Portuguese forces from Luanda defeated and killed King Antonio I of Kongo, setting off decades of civil war in the kingdom.
A fire in a bakery on Pudding Lane burned for four days and destroyed most of the medieval City, including old St Paul's (12 September New Style).
Louis XIV outlawed Protestant worship, and roughly 200,000 Huguenots fled abroad.

t: William of Orange lands at Torbay
n: William's landing at Brixham began the Glorious Revolution that removed James II; the date is Old Style (15 November New Style).
The Act allowed Protestant dissenters who took certain oaths to worship freely in licensed meeting houses (3 June New Style).
William III defeated James II near Drogheda; the date is Old Style (11 July New Style), and the battle is now marked on 12 July.

t: Peter the Great founds Saint Petersburg
n: Work began on the Peter and Paul Fortress on Hare Island in the Neva; Russia used the Julian calendar, and the New Style date is 27 May.

t: Ziegenbalg and Plutschau land at Tranquebar
n: The first Protestant missionaries to India arrived at the Danish colony, and Ziegenbalg later translated the New Testament into Tamil.
Christian David felled the first tree for a settlement on Count Zinzendorf's estate, which became the centre of the renewed Moravian Church.
A communion service brought renewal and reconciliation to the Herrnhut community, followed by a century-long round-the-clock prayer watch.

t: First Moravian missionaries reach St Thomas
n: Leonhard Dober and David Nitschmann arrived in the Danish West Indies to preach to enslaved Africans.
Listening to Luther's preface to Romans read aloud, Wesley felt his heart 'strangely warmed' (4 June New Style).

t: Whitefield's first open-air sermon at Kingswood
n: Whitefield preached in the open air to coal miners near Bristol, a key step in the field preaching of the Evangelical Revival; contemporaries wrote 1738/9 (28 February New Style).

t: Edwards preaches 'Sinners in the Hands of an Angry God'
n: Jonathan Edwards's sermon at Enfield became the best-known sermon of the Great Awakening (19 July New Style).

t: Premiere of Handel's Messiah in Dublin
n: The oratorio was first performed at the New Music Hall in Fishamble Street as a charity benefit (24 April New Style).
Government forces crushed Charles Edward Stuart's Jacobite army near Inverness (27 April New Style).
Cornwallis arrived at Chebucto with settlers to found Halifax, on land the Mi'kmaq had not ceded; this is the Old Style date (2 July New Style).

t: Britain and its colonies adopt the Gregorian calendar
n: Under the Calendar Act, Wednesday 2 September was followed by Thursday 14 September, and the legal year already began on 1 January.

t: Expulsion order read to the Acadians at Grand-Pre
n: Lt Col John Winslow read the deportation order to Acadian men gathered in the Grand-Pre church.
On All Saints' morning an earthquake, tsunami and fires destroyed most of Lisbon and shook European theology and philosophy.
Robert Clive's East India Company forces defeated Nawab Siraj ud-Daulah, starting British rule in Bengal.

t: Battle of the Plains of Abraham
n: Wolfe's British army defeated Montcalm's outside Quebec, and both generals were mortally wounded.
Burmese forces breached the walls after a 14-month siege and destroyed the Siamese capital.
Colonists protesting the Tea Act dumped 342 chests of East India Company tea into Boston Harbor.
Fighting between British regulars and colonial militia began the American Revolutionary War.
The Continental Congress in Philadelphia approved the final text declaring the thirteen colonies independent.
Preachers meeting at Lovely Lane Chapel in Baltimore organised the Methodist Episcopal Church and chose Asbury and Coke as superintendents.
Arthur Phillip raised the British flag at Sydney Cove, founding the convict colony of New South Wales on Aboriginal land.
Washington took the oath as the first President of the United States at Federal Hall.
A Paris crowd seized the royal fortress-prison, a defining moment of the French Revolution.
A nighttime gathering of enslaved people led by Dutty Boukman preceded the uprising that began the Haitian Revolution; the exact date rests on later accounts.

t: Baptist Missionary Society founded at Kettering
n: Twelve Baptist ministers, urged on by William Carey, formed the society in Widow Wallis's parlour, launching the modern missionary movement.
The deposed king was guillotined in the Place de la Revolution after the Convention convicted him of treason.
Carey and John Thomas reached Calcutta on a Danish ship after five months at sea; some accounts give 12 November.
Evangelical Anglicans of the Clapham circle formed the society at the Castle and Falcon inn in London to send missionaries to Africa and the East.
French soldiers found the stele at Rashid, and its parallel texts later allowed hieroglyphs to be deciphered; accounts differ between 15 and 19 July.

t: Serampore Mission established by Carey, Marshman and Ward
n: William Carey, Joshua Marshman and William Ward set up the Baptist mission at Danish Serampore, which went on to translate and print the Bible in many Indian languages.

t: British and Foreign Bible Society founded
n: The society was formed at the London Tavern to distribute the Scriptures without note or comment, becoming a model for Bible societies worldwide.
A British fleet under Nelson defeated the combined French and Spanish fleets off Cape Trafalgar; Nelson was killed in the action.

t: Adoniram and Ann Judson sail from Salem for Asia
n: Among the first American overseas missionaries, the Judsons left Salem on the brig Caravan; they later served for decades in Burma.
Napoleon's army and the Russian army under Kutuzov fought the bloodiest single day of the 1812 campaign west of Moscow (26 August Old Style).
Allied forces under Wellington and Prussian troops under Blücher defeated Napoleon, ending his final return to power.
Delegates from local Bible societies met in New York City and formed a national society to publish and distribute the Bible.
The line opened with George Stephenson's Locomotion No. 1 hauling the first train, the first public railway to use steam locomotives.
The British act abolishing slavery in most of the Empire, including British North America, came into force.
Samuel Morse sent the first official long-distance telegraph message from Washington to Baltimore, quoting Numbers 23:23.
George Williams and fellow drapery workers founded the Young Men's Christian Association for prayer and Bible study.
A new Executive Council answerable to the elected assembly was sworn in, the first responsible government in what is now Canada.
James Hudson Taylor left Liverpool aboard the Dumfries on his first voyage to China as a missionary.

t: First Fulton Street noon prayer meeting
n: Jeremiah Lanphier's lunchtime prayer meeting in New York grew into the widespread Prayer Meeting Revival of 1857-58.
On his third visit to St Catherine's Monastery, Constantin von Tischendorf was shown the bulk of the fourth-century Bible manuscript.

t: Darwin's On the Origin of Species published
n: Charles Darwin's book setting out the theory of evolution by natural selection was published in London.

t: Russia's Emancipation Manifesto frees the serfs
n: Tsar Alexander II signed the manifesto and statutes abolishing serfdom (19 February Old Style).

t: Bombardment of Fort Sumter opens the US Civil War
n: Confederate batteries fired on the federal fort in Charleston Harbor, beginning the American Civil War.
Delegates from the Maritimes and the Province of Canada met to discuss union, a first step toward Confederation.

t: Lee surrenders at Appomattox Court House
n: General Robert E. Lee surrendered the Army of Northern Virginia to Ulysses S. Grant, effectively ending the Civil War.

t: William Booth begins the East London mission
n: Booth's tent meetings in Whitechapel began the Christian Mission, renamed the Salvation Army in 1878.
Hudson Taylor and the first large group of China Inland Mission workers sailed from London on the clipper Lammermuir.
The British North America Act took effect, uniting Nova Scotia, New Brunswick and the Province of Canada as the Dominion of Canada.

t: Golden Spike completes US transcontinental railroad
n: The Central Pacific and Union Pacific lines were joined at Promontory Summit, Utah.
The canal linking the Mediterranean and the Red Sea was formally opened to shipping.
The First Vatican Council approved the constitution Pastor aeternus on papal primacy and infallibility.

t: Wreck of the SS Atlantic off Nova Scotia
n: The White Star liner struck rocks near Terence Bay in the early hours, with heavy loss of life; local residents rescued many survivors.

t: Bell makes the first telephone call
n: Alexander Graham Bell spoke to his assistant Thomas Watson over his new instrument in Boston.
A series of colossal explosions destroyed most of the volcanic island and generated deadly tsunamis.

t: Last spike of the Canadian Pacific Railway
n: Donald Smith drove the last spike at Craigellachie, completing Canada's first transcontinental railway.

t: First Zionist Congress opens in Basel
n: Theodor Herzl convened the congress that adopted the Basel Program calling for a Jewish home in the Land of Israel.
Three Christian commercial travelers formally organized the association later known for placing Bibles in hotels.

t: Agnes Ozman speaks in tongues at Topeka
n: At Charles Parham's Bethel Bible College, Ozman's experience became a starting point of modern Pentecostalism.

t: Marconi receives first transatlantic radio signal
n: At Signal Hill, St. John's, Marconi reported hearing the Morse letter S sent from Poldhu, Cornwall.
Orville and Wilbur Wright made the first controlled, sustained powered airplane flights at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina.

t: Evan Roberts' first revival meeting at Loughor
n: A small meeting of young people at Moriah chapel is generally regarded as the start of the 1904-05 Welsh Revival.
Troops fired on a peaceful procession of workers petitioning the tsar, sparking the 1905 Revolution (9 January Old Style).

t: Revival begins at Bonnie Brae Street, Los Angeles
n: Prayer meetings led by William J. Seymour broke out in tongues and soon moved to 312 Azusa Street, launching the Azusa Street Revival.
A major earthquake and the fires that followed destroyed much of San Francisco.

t: Silver Dart makes Canada's first powered flight
n: J.A.D. McCurdy flew the Aerial Experiment Association's Silver Dart over the ice of Bras d'Or Lake at Baddeck.

t: World Missionary Conference opens in Edinburgh
n: The gathering of Protestant mission societies is often seen as the starting point of the modern ecumenical movement.
The liner sank after striking an iceberg; many of the recovered victims were brought to Halifax and buried there.
Gavrilo Princip shot the heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne in Sarajevo, setting off the crisis that led to the First World War.
Britain's declaration brought Canada and the rest of the Empire into the First World War.
During the February Revolution the tsar signed his abdication at Pskov, ending Romanov rule (2 March Old Style).
All four divisions of the Canadian Corps attacked together and captured the ridge over the following days.
Foreign Secretary Arthur Balfour's letter to Lord Rothschild stated British support for a national home for the Jewish people in Palestine.
The Bolsheviks seized power from the Provisional Government; the Winter Palace fell overnight (25 October Old Style).
The munitions ship Mont-Blanc collided with the Imo in the Narrows and exploded, killing about 2,000 people and devastating north-end Halifax.
The British commander entered the Old City on foot through the Jaffa Gate after Ottoman forces withdrew.

t: Armistice ends fighting in the First World War
n: The armistice signed at Compiègne took effect at 11 a.m., ending hostilities on the Western Front.
The peace treaty between Germany and the Allied powers was signed in the Hall of Mirrors.
The fishing and racing schooner built by Smith and Rhuland went on to become an emblem of Nova Scotia.
Methodists, Congregationalists and most Presbyterians united at a service in Toronto's Mutual Street Arena.
The ocean immigration shed opened; about a million immigrants, refugees and war brides later entered Canada through it.
Panic selling on the New York Stock Exchange marked the deepest day of the 1929 crash and the onset of the Great Depression.
The Confessing Synod at Barmen affirmed the sole lordship of Christ over the church against state-imposed ideology.
Over the night of 9-10 November, synagogues, Jewish homes and businesses across Germany and Austria were attacked.
The German invasion began the Second World War in Europe.
In its first independent declaration of war, Canada entered the Second World War a week after Britain.
Japanese aircraft attacked the US Pacific Fleet in Hawaii, bringing the United States into the war.
Senior Nazi officials met near Berlin to coordinate the deportation and murder of Europe's Jews.
Allied forces, including Canadians at Juno Beach, landed in Normandy to open a western front.
Soviet troops reached the Auschwitz camp complex; the date is now International Holocaust Remembrance Day.
The Lutheran pastor and theologian, an opponent of the Nazi regime, was hanged at Flossenbürg concentration camp.
The Allies formally accepted Germany's unconditional surrender, ending the war in Europe.
A US aircraft dropped the first atomic bomb used in war on Hiroshima.

t: United Nations Charter enters into force
n: The UN came into existence once the Charter had been ratified by the required states; the date is marked as UN Day.

t: Viola Desmond refuses to leave a whites-only section
n: The Halifax businesswoman was arrested at New Glasgow's Roseland Theatre, a landmark in Canadian civil rights history.
British rule ended and India became independent, a day after Pakistan's creation, amid the partition of the subcontinent.

t: UN adopts the Partition Plan for Palestine
n: General Assembly Resolution 181 recommended dividing Mandatory Palestine into Jewish and Arab states with an international Jerusalem.
David Ben-Gurion proclaimed the State of Israel in Tel Aviv as the British Mandate ended.
The WCC was formally constituted at its first assembly in Amsterdam.

t: Universal Declaration of Human Rights adopted
n: The UN General Assembly in Paris adopted the declaration, drafted with Canadian John Humphrey's involvement.
Newfoundland became Canada's tenth province just before midnight on 31 March.

t: Billy Graham's Los Angeles campaign begins
n: The eight-week tent campaign brought Graham to national prominence.
Jim Elliot, Nate Saint and three colleagues were killed by Waorani men; family members later lived among the Waorani.
The Soviet Union put the first artificial satellite into orbit.
An underground 'bump' in the Springhill coal mine killed 75 miners; others were rescued after days underground.

t: Adolf Eichmann captured in Buenos Aires
n: Israeli agents seized the Holocaust organizer, who was later tried and executed in Israel.

t: Yuri Gagarin becomes the first human in space
n: Gagarin orbited Earth once aboard Vostok 1.

t: Construction of the Berlin Wall begins
n: East German authorities sealed the border between East and West Berlin overnight.
Pope John XXIII opened the council that reshaped Catholic liturgy and relations with other churches.
Kennedy was shot and killed in a motorcade in Dallas, Texas.
The new National Flag of Canada was officially inaugurated on Parliament Hill.

t: Israeli paratroopers reach the Temple Mount
n: During the Six-Day War, Israeli forces took the Old City; commander Motta Gur radioed "The Temple Mount is in our hands."
Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first humans to land on the Moon.

t: Lausanne Congress on World Evangelization opens
n: Some 2,700 evangelical leaders gathered and produced the Lausanne Covenant.
Israeli commandos rescued hostages from a hijacked airliner at Entebbe airport.
Egypt's Sadat and Israel's Begin signed frameworks for peace brokered by Jimmy Carter.
Queen Elizabeth II proclaimed the patriated constitution, including the Charter of Rights and Freedoms, in Ottawa.
Reactor No. 4 at the Chernobyl plant exploded, releasing radioactive material across Europe.
East Germany opened its border crossings, and crowds began crossing and dismantling the Wall.
In about 36 hours over 24-25 May, Israel flew some 14,000 Ethiopian Jews from Addis Ababa to Israel.
The Supreme Soviet's upper chamber voted the USSR out of existence, a day after Gorbachev resigned.
A methane and coal-dust explosion at Plymouth, Pictou County, killed all 26 miners underground.
Israel and the PLO signed the Declaration of Principles at the White House.
Meetings with Randy Clark began a long-running charismatic revival known as the Toronto Blessing.
Mandela became South Africa's first president elected in a fully representative democratic election.

t: Swissair Flight 111 crashes off Peggy's Cove
n: The MD-11 crashed into St. Margarets Bay after an in-flight fire, killing all 229 aboard.
The Lutheran World Federation and the Catholic Church signed a common statement on justification in Augsburg.
Hijacked airliners struck the World Trade Center and Pentagon; diverted flights landed in Gander and Halifax.
Juan made landfall near Halifax as a Category 2 hurricane, causing deaths and widespread damage.
A magnitude 9.1 earthquake off Sumatra generated tsunamis that killed about 230,000 people in many countries.
The Polish-born pope died after a pontificate of more than 26 years.
Steve Jobs unveiled the iPhone, which helped define the smartphone era.

t: Tohoku earthquake, tsunami and Fukushima accident
n: A magnitude 9.0 earthquake and tsunami killed nearly 20,000 people and triggered the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear accident.
The ATLAS and CMS experiments reported observing a new particle consistent with the Higgs boson.

t: Pope Benedict XVI's resignation takes effect
n: Benedict became the first pope in nearly six centuries to resign.
The World Health Organization characterized the COVID-19 outbreak as a pandemic.
Israel, the UAE and Bahrain signed normalization agreements at the White House.
An Ariane 5 rocket launched the telescope, built by NASA with ESA and the Canadian Space Agency.

t: Russia launches full-scale invasion of Ukraine
n: Russian forces invaded Ukraine on several fronts, beginning Europe's largest war since 1945.
The Queen of the United Kingdom and Canada died at Balmoral after a 70-year reign; Charles III succeeded her.

t: Post-tropical storm Fiona hits Nova Scotia
n: Fiona made landfall in eastern Nova Scotia, causing record low pressure and severe damage across Atlantic Canada.
A routine chapel service at Asbury University in Kentucky continued for about two weeks of round-the-clock worship.
Militants from Gaza killed about 1,200 people in southern Israel and took some 250 hostages, starting the Gaza war.
The cathedral reopened with a ceremony five years after the 2019 fire.

t: Fall of the Assad government in Syria
n: Opposition forces entered Damascus and Bashar al-Assad fled the country.

t: Mark Carney sworn in as prime minister
n: Carney succeeded Justin Trudeau as Canada's 24th prime minister.
The first Latin American pope died on Easter Monday at age 88.
Cardinal Robert Prevost was elected as the first pope from the United States.

t: Israel strikes Iran, beginning a twelve-day war
n: Israel attacked Iranian nuclear and military sites; a ceasefire took effect on 24 June.

t: Last living Israeli hostages released from Gaza
n: Under a ceasefire deal, Hamas freed the remaining 20 living hostages and Israel released Palestinian prisoners.

t: US strikes Venezuela and captures Maduro
n: US forces carried out strikes in Venezuela and took Nicolás Maduro into custody to face charges in New York.
The XXV Olympic Winter Games opened with a ceremony at Milan's San Siro stadium.

t: Ayatollah Khamenei killed in US-Israeli strikes
n: Iran's supreme leader was killed in strikes on the first day of a US-Israeli military campaign against Iran.

t: Artemis II launches crew around the Moon
n: NASA launched four astronauts, including Canadian Jeremy Hansen, on the first crewed lunar mission since 1972; they splashed down on 10 April.
Two major earthquakes caused thousands of deaths and widespread destruction.

t: Spain wins the 2026 FIFA World Cup
n: Spain beat Argentina 1-0 in the final of the first World Cup co-hosted by Canada, Mexico and the United States.
Close of the 12th Onah and the Age of Grace in this calendar's scheme.

t: First year of the Age of the Kingdom (6001 AM)
n: Start of the 13th Onah in this calendar's scheme.
